scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “An Almost-Linear Approximation Scheme for Edit Distance” (preprints/An-Almost-Linear-Approximation-Scheme-for-Edit-Distance-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 121 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7ecda63faaa7d6a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is one uniform randomized algorithm that, given x, y and a rational ε ∈ (0, 1), returns a nonnegative integer b D such that Pr  ED(x, y) ≤ b D ≤ (1 + ε) ED(x, y)  ≥ 2 3 . For every fixed rational ε, its worst-case expected running time on strings of total length N is N1+o(1) as N → ∞ on the logarithmic-word RAM. The expectation is over internal randomness only, and the bound includes input processing, preprocessing, numerical work, random sampling and all data-structure operations. Equal strings return zero deterministically.
